current_episode.title: Forum Focus Podcast: Well-Read Carpenter Cordell Sawyer Builds Successful Firm

guest.bio_context: Cordell Sawyer grew up in University City and worked as a janitor while reading books on wealth creation. He became one of the first apprentices to complete the carpenter's associate degree program through Balls Park Community College and was a union carpenter for 10 years before founding Sled Rock Construction in 2009 during the recession. He built his business by investing carpenter wages into real estate, leveraging that equity to bankroll his construction company.

3 years: Duration working on the Queenie Tower demolition project, Phase Two still wrapping up

pending_qa.q: What was the size and nature of the first commercial project for a startup construction firm?
pending_qa.r: The Love Travel Stop project on North Broadway in 2013 was the first commercial job, where the company performed most of the interior carpentry work. The team ran about eight guys and the project was valued at approximately $180,000 to $190,000, coming through a referral from the carpenters union.

pending_qa.q: What barriers do minority-owned construction companies face when entering new markets?
pending_qa.r: Cordell Sawyer explained that the natural assumption is that minority-owned small businesses do not know what they are doing, creating a significant hurdle to overcome. When bidding on work, he received no responses initially, and when feedback came, potential clients said they did not know his company. Being on a minority set-aside list does not automatically grant work—companies must first establish credibility and relationships, which requires additional effort beyond being qualified.

pending_qa.q: How can a small contractor build visibility and overcome the credibility gap in construction?
pending_qa.r: Cordell Sawyer turned the situation around by writing a strategic plan, joining trade organizations, attending all possible meetings and networking events to be in the room with decision-makers, and allowing them to know him personally. He emphasized that constantly making new relationships while leveraging existing ones has been the key to growth over his 11 years in business.

pending_qa.q: What are the most damaging payment term practices in the construction industry?
pending_qa.r: Cordell Sawyer identified 60, 90, and 120-day payment terms as standard in construction, which he called unfathomable and particularly harmful to small and emerging minority and women-owned businesses. He stressed that owners of large corporations understand how instrumental cash flow is to their own organizations and questioned why they do not apply the same logic when paying contractors.

pending_qa.q: What is the current workforce size and trajectory for a growing minority-owned construction contractor?
pending_qa.r: Sled Rock Construction expanded from specialty carpentry to small general contracting and became signatory to both carpenters and laborers unions. At the time of the interview, the company was running about 26 employees combined, and Cordell Sawyer stated his goal is to double that workforce within two to three years based on the trajectory and right connections.
